name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: To kick off our project, I think we should start by building packages, as this will give us a solid foundation to work from and allow us to organize our content in a logical way. By doing this first, we'll be able to create a clear structure for our tabs and elements to follow, making it easier to enrich and draft them later on. The trade-off I'm accepting here is that we'll be delaying the drafting of elements, which may seem like a pressing task, but I believe that having a well-organized package system will ultimately save us time and effort in the long run. This approach will also ensure that our final product is cohesive and easy to navigate, which aligns with our quality-first principle.

name: Vet
text: Vet — the skeptic — leans in: "Starting with packages *first* assumes we already know the structure we need—but what if the content itself dictates the organization? A better move might be to draft a few tabs and elements first, then let the natural relationships guide the package design. To settle this, we should compare: (1) a quick mockup of how tabs/elements *might* flow, versus (2) a proposed package hierarchy. The clearer vision wins."
